prediction.likelyOutcome: The trial court is likely to reject LBJ Venture's full ten-year acceleration theory because Section 10.02(b)'s acceleration remedy is textually conditioned on the landlord NOT reletting, and LBJ Venture did relet — pushing the rent award toward Kolaj's deficiency computation (around $96,000 inclusive of late fees and interest). The $300,000 kitchen claim is very likely to fail for lack of any competent valuation evidence at trial. Attorney's fees of roughly $50,000-$67,000 should be awarded given conceded liability and available fee-shifting under both the statute and the lease.

outcome.description: After the bench trial the trial court rendered judgment for the landlord of $96,072.49 (unpaid rent through trial net of replacement-tenant rent, late fees, and prejudgment interest) — the figure the tenant advocated, roughly one-tenth of the more than $900,000 the landlord sought — plus 18% post-judgment interest, and awarded $0 in attorneys' fees. The court of appeals affirmed the damages award and reversed only the denial of attorneys' fees, remanding for a determination of a reasonable fee under the lease.
outcome.finalNote: Damages affirmed; fee denial reversed and remanded.
